newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds firm in late trading.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds firm in late trading.

text.p: Argentine bonds remained firm in late trading Thursday and were seen closing the week on a steady note, dealers said.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 rose 1/8 to 94-1/4 while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2002 inched up $0.04 to 121.04.
"The market continues to look pretty strong although there isn't any fresh news to latch onto, other than the Bontes auction that was very good," one trader said.

The government sold $750 million in five-year Bonte Treasury bonds Thursday at a lower-than-expected cut-off yield of 8.58 percent. Bids totalled $4.32 billion, with a bid-to-cover ratio of 5.76 times.
"The market is calm and underpinned by the good performance of U.S. Treasuries and by strong local economic indicators, especially rising tax collection," another trader said.
